chapters.title: Hosea's Wife and Children
chapters.html:
Hosea 1

1The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

A Wife of Prostitution

2When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land has given itself to prostitution, turning away from the LORD."

3So he went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.

4The LORD said to him, "Call his name Jezreel, for in a little while I will punish the house of Jehu for the blood of Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.

5And it shall come to pass on that day that I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."

6She conceived again and bore a daughter, and the LORD said to him, "Call her name Lo-ruhamah, for I will no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, that I should ever forgive them.

7But I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them by the LORD their God. I will not save them by bow or sword or battle, by horses or horsemen."

8When she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived and bore a son.

9The LORD said, "Call his name Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I will not be yours."

Sons of the Living God

10Yet the number of the sons of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. And it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said to them, "You are not My people," it will be said to them, "Sons of the living God."

11The sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will be gathered together, and they will appoint for themselves one head and go up from the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.

Notes

  • v1 "Hosea son of Beeri" — Hoshea, from yasha, save, the name Moses gave Joshua before he changed it (Numbers 13:16). The kings of Judah run to Hezekiah, but the only king of Israel named is Jeroboam, though the book is spoken to Israel, the north. In the Hebrew text vv10–11 are 2:1–2; the English numbering is followed, and the Greek follows it too.

  • v2 "a wife of prostitution… the land has given itself to prostitution" — eshet zenunim, a wife of prostitutions, and zanoh tizneh ha-arets, the verb doubled, the land prostitutes itself greatly. The book's first command makes Hosea's marriage a picture of the land and its God. The text does not say whether Gomer was already a prostitute when he married her or became one after; a wife of prostitution can be read either way.

  • v4 "Jezreel… the blood of Jezreel… the house of Jehu" — Yizre'el, God sows. Jezreel was where Jehu killed the house of Ahab, and Kings records God's words to him after it: Because you have done well in doing what is right in My eyes… your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel (2 Kings 10:30). Here the same blood is laid to the account of Jehu's house. The name comes back as a promise: I will sow her for Myself in the land (2:23).

  • v6 "Lo-ruhamah… that I should ever forgive them" — Lo ruchamah, Not Shown Compassion, from racham, the word for a mother's womb and her love. Ki naso essa lahem, for lifting I will lift for them, is short and unclear: lift away their sin, that is, forgive them, which the verse refuses; or lift them away, take them away. The Greek has I will surely set myself against them.

  • v9 "Lo-ammi… I will not be yours" — Lo ammi, Not My People. Ve-anokhi lo ehyeh lakhem, and I, I will not be to you: ehyeh, I will be, is the name God gave Moses at the bush, I AM has sent me to you (Exodus 3:14). The words can be read I will not be yours, the covenant undone, or I am not I AM to you. The Greek has I am not yours.

  • v10 "like the sand of the sea… Sons of the living God" — the promise to Jacob, I will make your seed like the sand of the sea — too many to be counted (Genesis 32:12), set beside the sentence of v9 and reversing it. Paul quotes this verse of the Gentiles (Romans 9:26).

chapters.title: The Unfaithful Wife Won Back
chapters.html:
Hosea 2

1Say to your brothers, "Ammi," and to your sisters, "Ruhamah."

The Charge

2Contend with your mother, contend,
for she is not my wife,
and I am not her husband.
Let her put away her prostitution from her face,
and her adulteries from between her breasts,

3or I will strip her naked
and set her out as on the day she was born,
and make her like the wilderness,
and turn her into a parched land,
and kill her with thirst.

4On her children I will have no compassion,
for they are children of prostitution.

5For their mother has prostituted herself;
she who conceived them has acted shamefully.
For she said, "I will go after my lovers,
who give me my bread and my water,
my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."

6Therefore I am about to hedge up your way with thorns,
and I will build a wall against her,
so that she cannot find her paths.

7She will chase after her lovers but not overtake them;
she will seek them but not find them.
Then she will say, "I will go back to my first husband,
for it was better for me then than now."

8She did not know
that it was I who gave her the grain, the new wine and the oil,
and multiplied for her silver and gold,
which they used for Baal.

9Therefore I will take back My grain in its time
and My new wine in its season,
and I will snatch away My wool and My flax,
which were to cover her nakedness.

10Now I will uncover her shame
before the eyes of her lovers,
and no one will rescue her from My hand.

11I will put an end to all her rejoicing,
her feasts, her new moons, her sabbaths
and all her appointed feasts.

12I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees,
of which she said, "These are my wages,
which my lovers have given me."
I will make them a thicket,
and the beasts of the field will devour them.

13I will punish her for the days of the Baals,
when she burned incense to them
and adorned herself with her ring and her jewelry,
and went after her lovers,
and forgot Me, declares the LORD.

The Wilderness and the Door of Hope

14Therefore I am about to allure her,
and lead her into the wilderness,
and speak to her heart.

15There I will give her her vineyards,
and make the Valley of Achor a door of hope.
There she will answer as in the days of her youth,
as on the day she came up out of the land of Egypt.

16And it shall come to pass on that day, declares the LORD,
that you will call Me "My husband,"
and you will no longer call Me "My Baal."

17I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth,
and they will no longer be remembered by name.

18On that day I will make a covenant for them
with the beasts of the field, the birds of the heavens
and the creeping things of the ground;
I will break bow and sword and war from the land,
and make them lie down in safety.

19I will betroth you to Me forever;
I will betroth you to Me in righteousness and in justice,
in loyal love and in compassion.

20I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness,
and you will know the LORD.

21And it shall come to pass on that day
that I will answer, declares the LORD;
I will answer the heavens,
and they will answer the earth,

22and the earth will answer the grain, the new wine and the oil,
and they will answer Jezreel.

23I will sow her for Myself in the land,
and I will have compassion on Lo-ruhamah,
and I will say to Lo-ammi, "You are My people,"
and he will say, "My God."

Notes

  • v1 "Ammi… Ruhamah" — the names of 1:6 and 1:9 without their Lo, not: Ammi, My People, and Ruhamah, Shown Compassion. In the Hebrew text this verse is 2:3, and the chapter runs to 2:25; the English numbering is followed.

  • v2 "for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband" — the husband disowns her, yet the speech that follows does not let her go. The marriage of Hosea and Gomer (1:2–3) and the marriage of the LORD and the land are spoken of in the same voice, and the chapter moves from one to the other without marking it.

  • vv5, 8, 12 "my lovers, who give me my bread… which they used for Baal… These are my wages" — she thinks her food comes from her lovers; it came from the LORD (v8). Etnah, wages, a prostitute's pay, sounds like te'enah, fig tree: the fig trees she calls her wages are the ones He lays waste.

  • v14 "lead her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart" — the wilderness of the exodus, where it began (v15). Dibbarti al libbah, speak to her heart, is what Shechem did to Dinah (he spoke to the girl's heart, Genesis 34:3) and Joseph to his brothers (He comforted them and spoke to their heart, Genesis 50:21); Isaiah uses it for the comfort of Jerusalem, Speak to the heart of Jerusalem (Isaiah 40:2).

  • v15 "the Valley of Achor a door of hope" — Akhor, trouble, where Achan was stoned and the LORD turned from the heat of His anger (Joshua 7:26). The place named for Israel's first sin in the land becomes its entrance again. She will answer (anetah) begins the chain of answer in vv21–22.

  • v16 "My husband… My Baal" — ishi and ba'li, both my husband. Ba'al is the ordinary word for a husband or owner, and the name of the god; the LORD will not be called by it, so that the god's name is no longer in her mouth (v17).

  • v18 "a covenant… with the beasts of the field, the birds of the heavens" — as after the flood, God's covenant with every living soul… in the bird, in the beasts (Genesis 9:10), and bow and sword and war broken, where 1:5 broke only the bow of Israel.

  • vv19–20 "I will betroth you to Me" — erastikh, three times. Be- with this verb names the price the husband pays, as David betrothed Michal for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines (2 Samuel 3:14, be-me'ah). Here the price is righteousness and justice, loyal love and compassion, and faithfulness. Compassion, rachamim, is the word Lo-ruhamah was denied (1:6).

  • vv21–23 "I will answer… they will answer Jezreel. I will sow her" — heaven answers earth, earth answers the grain, the grain answers Jezreel, God sows, and God answers by sowing: u-zera'tiha, I will sow her. All three names of chapter 1 are undone in v23.

chapters.title: Bought Back
chapters.html:
Hosea 3

1The LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by a companion and is an adulteress, as the LORD loves the sons of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love cakes of raisins."

2So I bought her for myself for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.

3I said to her, "You are to stay with me for many days. You will not prostitute yourself or belong to any man, and I too will be so toward you."

4For the sons of Israel will stay many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or standing stone, without ephod or household gods.

5Afterward the sons of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king, and they will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the end of days.

Notes

  • v1 "a woman who is loved by a companion and is an adulteress" — ahuvat re'a. Re'a is a neighbor or a lover, and also a husband: Jeremiah says as a woman betrays her companion, so you have betrayed Me (Jeremiah 3:20). Read that way, the one who loves her is Hosea, as the LORD loves the sons of Israel though they turn to other gods; read the other way, she is loved by another man. The woman is not named, and the chapter does not say whether she is Gomer. The Greek reads the same letters as ra', evil: a woman who loves evil things. Cakes of raisins were a festival food, given out by David when the ark came to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:19); here they go with the other gods.

  • v2 "fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley" — va-ekkereha, I bought her, from a rare verb of buying. Shekels is not in the Hebrew, which has fifteen of silver. The lethech is a measure found only here, and its size is not given. The Greek has a homer of barley and a jar of wine.

  • v3 "and I too will be so toward you" — ve-gam ani elayikh, and also I toward you: four words with no verb. They can mean that he will keep himself for her as she keeps herself for him, or that he too will stay away from her for those days, as Israel will be without its king and its sacrifices (v4).

  • v4 "without ephod or household gods" — teraphim, the gods Rachel stole from Laban (Genesis 31:19). The list sets what the law allowed beside what it forbade: king and prince, sacrifice and ephod, with the standing stone the law rules out, You shall not set up for yourself a standing stone (Deuteronomy 16:22), and the teraphim. All of them are taken away together.

  • v5 "David their king… in the end of days" — a king of David's line, as Ezekiel says, My servant David will be king over them (Ezekiel 37:24). In the end of days, be-acharit ha-yamim, is Jacob's phrase (Genesis 49:1).

chapters.title: The LORD's Case Against the Land
chapters.html:
Hosea 4

No Knowledge of God

1Hear the word of the LORD, sons of Israel,
for the LORD has a case against the inhabitants of the land:
there is no faithfulness, no loyal love,
and no knowledge of God in the land.

2Swearing and lying, murder and stealing and adultery break out,
and bloodshed follows bloodshed.

3Therefore the land mourns,
and all who live in it waste away,
with the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens;
even the fish of the sea are taken away.

Like People, Like Priest

4Yet let no one bring a case, and let no one rebuke,
for your people are like those who contend with the priest.

5You will stumble by day,
and the prophet will stumble with you by night,
and I will destroy your mother.

6My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
Because you have rejected knowledge,
I reject you from being a priest to Me;
since you have forgotten the law of your God,
I also will forget your children.

7The more they increased, the more they sinned against Me;
I will exchange their glory for shame.

8They feed on the sin of My people,
and they set their hearts on their iniquity.

9It will be the same for the people as for the priest:
I will punish them for their ways
and repay them for their deeds.

10They will eat but not be satisfied;
they will give themselves to prostitution but not increase,
for they have stopped heeding the LORD.

A Spirit of Prostitution

11Prostitution, wine and new wine take away the understanding.

12My people consult their piece of wood,
and their staff gives them answers;
for a spirit of prostitution has led them astray,
and they have prostituted themselves, leaving their God.

13On the tops of the mountains they sacrifice,
and on the hills they burn incense,
under oak and poplar and terebinth,
because their shade is good.
Therefore your daughters prostitute themselves,
and your brides commit adultery.

14I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves,
nor your brides when they commit adultery;
for the men themselves go aside with prostitutes
and sacrifice with consecrated women,
and a people without understanding comes to ruin.

15Though you prostitute yourself, Israel,
let Judah not become guilty.
Do not go to Gilgal,
do not go up to Beth-aven,
and do not swear, "As the LORD lives."

16For Israel is as stubborn as a stubborn heifer;
now will the LORD pasture them
like a lamb in a broad place?

17Ephraim is joined to idols;
let him alone.

18When their drink is gone, they give themselves to prostitution;
her rulers love shame above all.

19A wind has wrapped her up in its wings,
and they will be ashamed of their sacrifices.

Notes

  • v1 "the LORD has a case… no knowledge of God" — riv, a case brought in court. The charge names three things missing: emet, faithfulness; chesed, loyal love, the word of the betrothal in 2:19; and da'at Elohim, knowledge of God. Knowledge comes back twice in v6, and da'at is the root of the betrothal's last line, you will know the LORD (2:20).

  • v2 "Swearing and lying, murder and stealing and adultery" — five verbs in a row with no subject, three of them the words of the Ten Commandments: You shall not murder… commit adultery… steal (Exodus 20:13–15). Jeremiah makes the same list at the temple gate (Jeremiah 7:9).

  • v3 "the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens; even the fish of the sea" — the creatures of the covenant promised in 2:18, the beasts of the field, the birds of the heavens, now wasting with the land; and the fish, which no promise named.

  • vv4–6 "like those who contend with the priest… I will destroy your mother… My people are destroyed" — v4 is obscure: the words say the people are like those who contend with a priest, the man the law condemns for not listening to the priest (Deuteronomy 17:12), and then the speech turns on the priest himself (you, vv4–9). Damiti, I will destroy, and nidmu, are destroyed, are the same verb, one verse apart: the priest's mother and My people go down together.

  • v7 "I will exchange their glory for shame" — kevodam be-qalon amir, the verb of the psalm and of Jeremiah: They exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox (Psalm 106:20); My people have exchanged their Glory for what does not profit (Jeremiah 2:11). There the people exchanged their Glory; here the LORD makes the exchange.

  • vv8–9 "They feed on the sin of My people… the same for the people as for the priest" — chattat is both sin and sin offering, which the priest was to eat: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it (Leviticus 6:26). The more the people sin, the more the priests eat. Kha-am ka-kohen is Isaiah's line for a judgment that spares no rank: It will be the same for the people as for the priest (Isaiah 24:2).

  • v12 "their piece of wood… their staff… leaving their God" — etso, his wood, an idol or a sacred tree, and maqlo, his staff, cast to find an answer. Va-yiznu mi-tachat Eloheihem, they prostituted themselves from under their God, is the phrase of the law of the wife suspected of adultery, if you have gone astray while under your husband (Numbers 5:20).

  • v14 "consecrated women" — qedeshot, the word Judah's friend used when he looked for Tamar, Where is the consecrated woman (Genesis 38:21), and which the law forbids, There shall be no consecrated woman among the daughters of Israel (Deuteronomy 23:17). The fathers are blamed for what the daughters do.

  • v15 "Gilgal… Beth-aven" — Beit Aven, House of Wickedness, a town near Beth-aven, east of Bethel (Joshua 7:2). In 10:5 Hosea speaks of the calves of Beth-aven, and the calf stood at Bethel (1 Kings 12:29), House of God: the name puts aven, wickedness, in the place of God.

  • vv16–19 the end of the chapter — Ephraim, the tribe of Joseph's younger son, stands for the whole northern kingdom from here on. The last three verses are among the hardest in the book. Now will the LORD pasture them like a lamb in a broad place? (v16) can also be read as a statement, the LORD letting a stubborn heifer graze alone in the open. In v18 the Hebrew runs their drink has turned… they love, give! shame, her shields: each word is clear, the sentence is not.

chapters.title: A Snare at Mizpah, and a Lion to Ephraim
chapters.html:
Hosea 5

Judgment on Priests and King

1Hear this, priests!
Pay attention, house of Israel!
Listen, house of the king!
For the judgment is for you,
because you have been a snare at Mizpah
and a net spread out on Tabor.

2They have gone deep in slaughter at Shittim,
but I will discipline them all.

3I know Ephraim,
and Israel is not hidden from Me;
for now, Ephraim, you have prostituted yourself;
Israel is defiled.

4Their deeds do not let them
return to their God,
for a spirit of prostitution is within them,
and they do not know the LORD.

5The pride of Israel testifies against him to his face;
Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity,
and Judah also stumbles with them.

6With their flocks and their herds
they will go to seek the LORD,
but they will not find Him;
He has withdrawn from them.

7They have dealt faithlessly with the LORD,
for they have borne strange children.
Now the new moon will devour them with their portions.

Sound the Alarm

8Blow the horn in Gibeah,
the trumpet in Ramah!
Sound the alarm at Beth-aven:
"After you, Benjamin!"

9Ephraim will become a desolation
on the day of rebuke;
among the tribes of Israel
I make known what is sure.

10The princes of Judah have become
like those who move a boundary marker;
on them I will pour out My wrath like water.

11Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment,
because he was determined to go after rule.

12But I am like a moth to Ephraim,
and like rot to the house of Judah.

13When Ephraim saw his sickness,
and Judah his wound,
Ephraim went to Assyria
and sent to King Jareb;
but he cannot heal you
or cure you of your wound.

14For I will be like a lion to Ephraim,
and like a young lion to the house of Judah.
I Myself will tear and go away;
I will carry off, and no one will rescue.

15I will go and return to My place
until they acknowledge their guilt and seek My face;
in their distress they will seek Me at dawn.

Notes

  • v1 "the judgment is for you… a snare at Mizpah and a net spread out on Tabor" — lakhem ha-mishpat, to you is the judgment: the sentence is against them, and judging was also their task. Mizpah and Tabor are two heights, and the priests and the king are the hunter's trap set on them.

  • v2 "They have gone deep in slaughter at Shittim" — ve-shachatah setim he'emiqu, three words that are hard to put together. Setim can be the place Shittim, where Israel began to whore with the daughters of Moab and ate at the sacrifices of their gods (Numbers 25:1–2), set beside Mizpah and Tabor; or the word for those who turn aside, rebels. Shachatah is slaughter, the killing of animals for sacrifice. The Greek reads the line differently: which those who hunt the prey have fixed.

  • v5 "The pride of Israel testifies against him to his face" — ge'on Yisra'el can be Israel's own arrogance, which speaks against him, or the One who is Israel's pride. The same words come again in 7:10.

  • v8 "After you, Benjamin!" — acharekha Binyamin, the call of Deborah's song, after you, Benjamin, with your kinsmen (Judges 5:14). Gibeah and Ramah are towns of Benjamin (Joshua 18:25, 28).

  • v10 "like those who move a boundary marker" — the law's curse, Cursed is he who moves his neighbor's boundary marker (Deuteronomy 27:17).

  • v11 "because he was determined to go after rule" — tsav, rule, is found again only in Isaiah's mocking rule upon rule, rule upon rule (Isaiah 28:10, 13). What rule Ephraim followed is not said. The Greek has vanities.

  • v13 "King Jareb" — melekh yarev, King He-Contends. The words read like a nickname, and no king of Assyria by that name is known in the Bible; the Greek also takes it as a name, Iareim. It comes again in 10:6.

  • vv13–14; 6:1 "he cannot heal you… I will tear… He has torn, and He will heal us" — rafa, heal, and taraf, tear: Assyria cannot heal, the LORD is the lion who tears, and in 6:1 the people say He who tore will heal. The two verbs share two of their three letters, r and p.

  • v15 "they will seek Me at dawn" — yeshacharununi, from shachar, dawn, the word of the people's answer, His going out is as sure as the dawn (6:3).

chapters.title: On the Third Day
chapters.html:
Hosea 6

Come, Let Us Return

1"Come, let us return to the LORD;
for He has torn, and He will heal us;
He has struck, and He will bind us up.

2He will revive us after two days;
on the third day He will raise us up,
that we may live before Him.

3Let us know, let us press on to know the LORD;
His going out is as sure as the dawn.
He will come to us like the rain,
like the spring rain that waters the earth."

Your Loyal Love Is Like a Morning Cloud

4What shall I do with you, Ephraim?
What shall I do with you, Judah?
Your loyal love is like a morning cloud,
like the dew that goes early away.

5Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets;
I have killed them by the words of My mouth;
and My judgment goes out like light.

6For I desire loyal love and not sacrifice,
the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.

7But like Adam they have broken the covenant;
there they dealt faithlessly with Me.

8Gilead is a city of evildoers,
tracked with blood.

9As bandits lie in wait for a man,
so a band of priests
murders on the road to Shechem;
they have done what is vile.

10In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing:
there is Ephraim's prostitution;
Israel is defiled.

11For you also, Judah, a harvest is appointed,
when I restore the fortunes of My people.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "Come, let us return to the LORD" — the people's words, answering 5:14–15: He is the lion who tore, and they say He will heal. Whether the chapter accepts their words is the question of v4, What shall I do with you, Ephraim? Their loyal love lasts like a morning cloud.

  • v2 "on the third day He will raise us up" — ba-yom ha-shelishi yeqimenu, said of the people, two days and then the third. The Gospels say Jesus would on the third day be raised (Matthew 16:21), and Paul names the third day as what the Scriptures said (1 Corinthians 15:4).

  • v5 "and My judgment goes out like light" — this follows the Greek, kai to krima mou hōs phōs exeleusetai. The Hebrew letters are the same, divided differently: u-mishpatekha or yetse, and your judgments, light goes out. The verses around it are all I and My: I have hewn… I have killed… the words of My mouth.

  • v6 "For I desire loyal love and not sacrifice" — chesed, the word of v4, where Israel's loyal love vanished like dew. Samuel said it before, To listen is better than sacrifice (1 Samuel 15:22). Jesus quotes the verse twice in Matthew from the Greek, which has eleos, mercy: I desire mercy, not sacrifice (Matthew 9:13; 12:7).

  • v7 "But like Adam they have broken the covenant; there" — ke-adam is like Adam or like mankind. Job uses the same words, if I have covered my transgressions as Adam did (Job 31:33). The Greek has like a man. The there that follows asks for a place, and the next verses name places, Gilead and Shechem; a town called Adam stood on the Jordan, Adam, the city beside Zarethan (Joshua 3:16), but the Hebrew has like, not at.

  • v8 "tracked with blood" — aqubbah mi-dam, heel-marked with blood, from aqev, heel, the word that gave Jacob his name (Genesis 25:26). Hosea comes back to it in 12:3.

  • v10 "a horrible thing" — sha'arurriyyah, the word Jeremiah uses, in the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: they commit adultery (Jeremiah 23:14).

  • v11 "when I restore the fortunes of My people" — be-shuvi shevut ammi, the promise of Jeremiah, I will restore your fortunes (Jeremiah 29:14). The line runs straight on into 7:1, when I would heal Israel.

chapters.title: An Oven, a Cake Not Turned, a Silly Dove
chapters.html:
Hosea 7

Like an Oven

1When I would heal Israel,
the iniquity of Ephraim is uncovered,
and the evil deeds of Samaria;
for they practice deceit:
the thief breaks in,
and a band of raiders plunders in the street.

2But they do not say to themselves
that I remember all their evil.
Now their deeds surround them;
they are before My face.

3With their evil they make the king glad,
and the princes with their lies.

4They are all adulterers;
they are like an oven heated by a baker,
who stops stirring the fire
from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.

5On the day of our king
the princes made him sick with the heat of wine;
he stretched out his hand with scoffers.

6For they come near with their hearts like an oven
as they lie in wait;
all night their baker sleeps;
in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.

7All of them are hot as an oven,
and they devour their rulers;
all their kings have fallen,
and not one of them calls to Me.

Ephraim Mixes with the Peoples

8Ephraim mixes himself among the peoples;
Ephraim is a cake not turned.

9Strangers devour his strength,
and he does not know it;
gray hairs are sprinkled on him,
and he does not know it.

10The pride of Israel testifies against him to his face;
yet they do not return to the LORD their God,
or seek Him, for all this.

11Ephraim has become like a dove,
silly and without sense;
they call to Egypt,
they go to Assyria.

12As they go, I will spread My net over them;
I will bring them down like the birds of the heavens;
I will discipline them as their congregation has been told.

13Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me!
Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against Me!
I would redeem them,
but they speak lies against Me.

14They do not cry to Me from their heart
when they wail on their beds;
for grain and new wine they gash themselves;
they turn away from Me.

15Though I trained and strengthened their arms,
they plot evil against Me.

16They turn, but not upward;
they are like a deceitful bow.
Their princes will fall by the sword
for the fury of their tongue;
this will be their derision in the land of Egypt.

Notes

  • v1 "When I would heal Israel" — the sentence begins at the end of chapter 6, when I restore the fortunes of My people (6:11). Heal is the verb of 5:13 and 6:1: Assyria could not heal, the people said the LORD would, and when He comes to heal, what He finds is their iniquity.

  • vv4–8 the oven and the cake — one picture from the baker's trade: a heated oven left to smoulder all night while the dough rises, then blazing up in the morning, as the princes' plots smoulder and then burst out at the king. The lines are compressed and hard to follow word by word (vv4–6), and the Greek reads several of them differently. Yitbolal, mixes himself, is the verb for flour mixed with oil in the grain offering (Leviticus 2:4), and a cake not turned is burnt on one side and raw on the other.

  • v7 "all their kings have fallen" — Kings records four kings of Israel struck down by the men who took their thrones: Shallum conspired against him and struck him down (2 Kings 15:10), Menahem struck down Shallum (15:14), Pekah conspired against him (15:25), and Hoshea made a conspiracy against Pekah (15:30).

  • v10 "The pride of Israel testifies against him to his face" — the words of 5:5, said again.

  • v11 "like a dove, silly and without sense… Egypt… Assyria" — pothah, easily led. The north turned to both powers in turn: the last king, Hoshea, had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and stopped the tribute he had paid Assyria year by year (2 Kings 17:4).

  • v13 "I would redeem them" — ve-anokhi efdem, the verb of the exodus, redeemed you from the house of slaves (Deuteronomy 7:8).

  • v14 "for grain and new wine they gash themselves" — this follows the Greek, katetemnonto, they cut themselves, which reads yitgodadu. The Hebrew has yitgoraru, one letter different, they gather themselves or they stir themselves up. Gashing is the rite of the prophets of Baal, who gashed themselves… until the blood gushed out (1 Kings 18:28), and the law forbids it, You shall not gash yourselves (Deuteronomy 14:1).

  • v16 "They turn, but not upward… a deceitful bow" — yashuvu lo al, they return, not on high: obscure; al is above, and the words may mean they turn to what is not God. A deceitful bow, one that springs aside when it is drawn, is the psalm's picture of Israel in the wilderness, they twisted like a deceitful bow (Psalm 78:57).

chapters.title: They Sow the Wind
chapters.html:
Hosea 8

The Calf of Samaria

1Set the horn to your lips!
One comes like an eagle over the house of the LORD,
because they have broken My covenant
and rebelled against My law.

2To Me they cry,
"My God, we know You — we, Israel!"

3Israel has rejected the good;
the enemy will pursue him.

4They made kings, but not through Me;
they made princes, but I did not know it.
With their silver and their gold
they made idols for themselves,
to be cut off.

5Your calf is rejected, Samaria;
My anger burns against them.
How long will they be incapable of innocence?

6For it is from Israel:
a craftsman made it,
and it is not God;
the calf of Samaria will be broken to splinters.

Sowing the Wind

7For they sow the wind,
and they will reap the whirlwind.
The standing grain has no head;
the sprout will yield no flour;
and if it does yield,
strangers will swallow it up.

8Israel is swallowed up;
now they are among the nations
like a jar no one wants.

9For they have gone up to Assyria,
a wild donkey wandering alone;
Ephraim has hired lovers.

10Even though they hire among the nations,
I will now gather them up,
and they will soon writhe
under the burden of the king of princes.

Altars for Sinning

11Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning,
they have become to him altars for sinning.

12Were I to write for him the many things of My law,
they would be counted as something strange.

13As for the sacrifices of My gifts,
they sacrifice flesh and eat it,
but the LORD does not accept them.
Now He will remember their iniquity
and punish their sins;
they will return to Egypt.

14Israel has forgotten his Maker
and built palaces,
and Judah has multiplied fortified cities;
but I will send fire on his cities,
and it will devour her strongholds.

Notes

  • v1 "like an eagle over the house of the LORD" — ka-nesher, the curse of the law: a nation from far away… swooping as the eagle swoops (Deuteronomy 28:49).

  • vv2–3 "My God, we know You… Israel has rejected the good" — the cry claims the knowledge of God that 4:1 found missing. Zanach, rejected, comes again in v5: Israel has rejected the good, and the calf is rejected.

  • v4 "They made kings, but not through Me" — himlikhu… hesiru, made kings… made princes; the second verb can also be heard as removed, the way kings were set up and struck down (7:7). To be cut off closes the verse without a subject: the idols, or Israel with them.

  • vv5–6 "Your calf… a craftsman made it, and it is not God" — the calf of the north, which Jeroboam set up with the words of Aaron's calf: These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt (1 Kings 12:28). Shevavim, splinters, is found only here.

  • v7 "they sow the wind, and they will reap the whirlwind… the sprout will yield no flour" — tsemach beli ya'aseh qemach, a rhyme in Hebrew, sprout… flour. Zera, sow, is the root of Jezreel (1:4; 2:23): what God sows bears, and what Israel sows is wind.

  • v8 "like a jar no one wants" — ki-khli ein chefets bo, the words Jeremiah uses of King Coniah, a jar no one wants (Jeremiah 22:28).

  • v9 "a wild donkey wandering alone… Ephraim" — pere, wild donkey, sounds like Efrayim. It is what Ishmael was to be, a wild donkey of a man (Genesis 16:12). Hitnu ahavim, they have hired lovers, is the reverse of the prostitute's wages of 2:12: here Ephraim pays.

  • v10 "they will soon writhe under the burden of the king of princes" — va-yachellu me'at mi-massa: obscure. Yachellu can be begin, or writhe as in labor; massa is a burden or a tribute. The Greek reads they will cease a little from anointing king and princes.

  • v13 "they will return to Egypt" — the exodus run backward: the people brought out of Egypt go back to it (9:3; 11:5).

  • v14 "I will send fire on his cities, and it will devour her strongholds" — the refrain Amos uses against every nation in turn (Amos 1:4–2:5).

chapters.title: No Birth, No Womb, No Conception
chapters.html:
Hosea 9

Unclean Bread in Exile

1Do not rejoice, Israel;
do not exult like the peoples,
for you have prostituted yourself, leaving your God;
you have loved a prostitute's wages
on every threshing floor of grain.

2Threshing floor and winepress will not feed them,
and the new wine will fail her.

3They will not stay in the land of the LORD;
Ephraim will return to Egypt,
and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.

4They will not pour out wine to the LORD,
and their sacrifices will not please Him.
To them it will be like mourners' bread:
all who eat it are defiled;
for their bread will be for their hunger only;
it will not go into the house of the LORD.

5What will you do on the day of the appointed feast,
on the day of the LORD's feast?

6For they are going away from destruction;
Egypt will gather them,
Memphis will bury them.
Nettles will take possession of their precious things of silver;
thorns will be in their tents.

The Prophet Is a Fool

7The days of punishment have come;
the days of repayment have come;
Israel will know it.
"The prophet is a fool,
the man of the spirit is mad" —
because of the greatness of your iniquity
and great hostility.

8Ephraim is a watchman with my God;
the prophet — a fowler's snare is on all his ways,
and hostility in the house of his God.

9They have gone deep in corruption
as in the days of Gibeah;
He will remember their iniquity;
He will punish their sins.

Ephraim Will Bear No Fruit

10Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel;
like the first fruit on the fig tree in its first season
I saw your fathers.
But they came to Baal-peor
and consecrated themselves to the Shame,
and they became loathsome like what they loved.

11Ephraim — their glory will fly away like a bird:
no birth, no womb, no conception.

12Even if they bring up their children,
I will bereave them until none is left.
Woe to them indeed
when I turn away from them!

13Ephraim, as I saw him, was like Tyre,
planted in a meadow;
but Ephraim must bring out his children to the slayer.

14Give them, O LORD —
what will You give?
Give them a miscarrying womb
and dry breasts.

15All their evil is in Gilgal;
there I came to hate them.
Because of the evil of their deeds
I will drive them out of My house;
I will love them no more;
all their princes are rebels.

16Ephraim is struck;
their root is dried up;
they will bear no fruit.
Even if they give birth,
I will kill the beloved fruit of their womb.

17My God will reject them,
because they have not listened to Him;
and they will be wanderers among the nations.

Notes

  • v1 "you have loved a prostitute's wages on every threshing floor of grain" — etnan, the wage the law will not let into the sanctuary, You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute… into the house of the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 23:18). The threshing floors are where the harvest was celebrated, and the harvest is what she thought her lovers paid her (2:5, 12).

  • vv3–4 "unclean food… like mourners' bread" — Ezekiel was told the same, This is how the sons of Israel will eat their bread unclean among the nations (Ezekiel 4:13). Lechem onim, bread of mourners, is the bread of a house where someone has died, unfit for offering: a farmer giving his tithe had to swear, I have not eaten of it in my mourning (Deuteronomy 26:14).

  • v6 "Memphis will bury them" — Mof, the city of Egypt Jeremiah names, The men of Memphis and Tahpanhes (Jeremiah 2:16). Those who flee the destruction at home find a grave in Egypt.

  • v7 "The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad" — meshugga, mad, the word Jehu's officers used of the young prophet who anointed him, Why did this madman come to you? (2 Kings 9:11). The line may be the people's mockery of the prophet, or the LORD's verdict on prophets who fail; the verse gives no speaker.

  • v8 "Ephraim is a watchman with my God; the prophet" — obscure. Tsofeh, watchman, is the prophet's title, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel (Ezekiel 3:17); the line can mean that the prophet is the watchman and the people set snares for him.

  • v9 "as in the days of Gibeah" — the crime of Gibeah, when a Levite's secondary wife was abused to death and everyone who saw it would say, "Nothing like this has happened or been seen" (Judges 19:30).

  • v10 "Like grapes in the wilderness… Baal-peor… the Shame" — the LORD remembers finding Israel as a traveler finds grapes in the desert; then Israel yoked itself to Baal of Peor (Numbers 25:3). Boshet, the Shame, stands in place of Baal's name, as in Jeremiah, the altars you have set up to the Shame, altars to burn incense to Baal (Jeremiah 11:13). Va-yinnazeru, consecrated themselves, is the verb of the Nazirite.

  • vv11–16 Ephraim and fruit — Efrayim was named for fruit: God has made me fruitful (Genesis 41:52). Now the name is undone: no birth, no womb, no conception; they will bear no fruit, peri (v16). The prayer of v14 takes back Jacob's blessing on Joseph, Ephraim's father, blessings of breasts and womb (Genesis 49:25).

  • v15 "I will drive them out of My house… all their princes are rebels" — garash, the verb of a wife sent away, a woman divorced from her husband (Leviticus 21:7). Sareihem sorerim, their princes, rebels, is a pun Isaiah also makes, Your rulers are rebels (Isaiah 1:23).

  • v17 "wanderers among the nations" — nodedim, the root of Cain's sentence, A wanderer and a wavering one you shall be in the earth (Genesis 4:12).

The Prophet Is a Fool

The days of punishment have come; the days of repayment have come; Israel will know it. "The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad" — because of the greatness of your iniquity and great hostility.
Ephraim is a watchman with my God; the prophet — a fowler's snare is on all his ways, and hostility in the house of his God.
They have gone deep in corruption as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their iniquity; He will punish their sins.
Ephraim Will Bear No Fruit

Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like the first fruit on the fig tree in its first season I saw your fathers. But they came to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to the Shame, and they became loathsome like what they loved.
Ephraim — their glory will fly away like a bird: no birth, no womb, no conception.
Even if they bring up their children, I will bereave them until none is left. Woe to them indeed when I turn away from them!
Ephraim, as I saw him, was like Tyre, planted in a meadow; but Ephraim must bring out his children to the slayer.
Give them, O LORD — what will You give? Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
All their evil is in Gilgal; there I came to hate them. Because of the evil of their deeds I will drive them out of My house; I will love them no more; all their princes are rebels.
Ephraim is struck; their root is dried up; they will bear no fruit. Even if they give birth, I will kill the beloved fruit of their womb.
My God will reject them, because they have not listened to Him; and they will be wanderers among the nations.

chapters.title: Break Up Your Fallow Ground
chapters.html:
Hosea 10

The Calf Carried to Assyria

1Israel is a spreading vine
that yields its fruit.
The more his fruit increased,
the more altars he built;
the better his land,
the better he made his standing stones.

2Their heart is false;
now they must bear their guilt.
He will break the neck of their altars
and destroy their standing stones.

3For now they will say,
"We have no king,
for we did not fear the LORD;
and the king — what could he do for us?"

4They speak words,
swearing falsely in making covenants;
so judgment springs up like poison
in the furrows of the field.

5The inhabitants of Samaria will be in dread
for the calf of Beth-aven;
its people will mourn over it,
and its idol priests, who rejoiced over it,
over its glory,
for it has gone into exile from it.

6The calf itself will be carried to Assyria
as tribute to King Jareb.
Ephraim will take shame,
and Israel will be ashamed of his own counsel.

7Samaria and her king will perish
like a twig on the face of the waters.

8The high places of Aven, the sin of Israel,
will be destroyed;
thorn and thistle will grow up on their altars.
They will say to the mountains, "Cover us,"
and to the hills, "Fall on us."

Sow Righteousness

9Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel;
there they have stood.
Will not war overtake them in Gibeah
against the sons of injustice?

10When I desire, I will discipline them;
and peoples will be gathered against them
when they are bound for their double iniquity.

11Ephraim was a trained heifer
that loved to thresh,
and I spared her fair neck;
but I will harness Ephraim;
Judah must plow;
Jacob must harrow for himself.

12Sow for yourselves righteousness;
reap according to loyal love;
break up your fallow ground;
for it is time to seek the LORD,
until He comes and rains righteousness on you.

13You have plowed wickedness;
you have reaped injustice;
you have eaten the fruit of lies.
Because you have trusted in your own way,
in the multitude of your mighty men,

14the roar of battle will rise among your people,
and all your fortresses will be destroyed,
as Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel on the day of battle,
when mothers were dashed to pieces on top of their children.

15So it will be done to you, Bethel,
because of your great wickedness.
At dawn the king of Israel
will be utterly cut off.

Notes

  • v1 "a spreading vine that yields its fruit" — gefen boqeq. Baqaq elsewhere means lay waste, empty, as in Isaiah's The LORD is about to empty the earth (Isaiah 24:1), and boqeq can be read as a plundered vine; the Greek reads a well-branched vine, and the rest of the verse is about plenty. The psalm sings of the vine: You brought a vine out of Egypt (Psalm 80:8). Peri, fruit, is the sound of Ephraim's name again (9:16).

  • vv1–2 "their standing stones… He will break the neck of their altars" — ya'arof, the verb of the law for a firstborn donkey not redeemed, you shall break its neck (Exodus 13:13). Chalaq libbam, their heart is smooth, is false, flattering; it can also be read divided.

  • v4 "judgment springs up like poison" — rosh, a poisonous plant, the word of the law's warning against a root bearing poison and wormwood (Deuteronomy 29:18). Justice, which should feed the land, comes up as a weed in the plowed rows.

  • vv5–6 "its glory… has gone into exile from it" — kevodo ki galah mimmennu, the words of the dying mother who named her son Ichabod: The glory has gone into exile from Israel (1 Samuel 4:21). There the glory was the ark of God; here it is a calf, carried to Assyria as tribute. Kemarim, idol priests, is the word for the priests Josiah put down (2 Kings 23:5).

  • v8 "thorn and thistle… Cover us… Fall on us" — qots ve-dardar, the curse on the ground in Eden, Thorn and thistle it shall sprout for you (Genesis 3:18). Jesus quotes the cry to the mountains on the way to the cross (Luke 23:30), and Revelation has it again (Revelation 6:16).

  • vv9–10 "the days of Gibeah… their double iniquity" — Gibeah again (9:9), where Israel's war against the town began (Judges 20). The lines are obscure: there they have stood may mean they have stayed in that sin ever since. What the double iniquity is, the text does not say.

  • v11 "a trained heifer that loved to thresh… Judah must plow" — a threshing animal walks free over the grain and eats as it goes, You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing (Deuteronomy 25:4); now Ephraim is put under the yoke for the hard work of plowing.

  • v12 "break up your fallow ground… rains righteousness on you" — Jeremiah says it to Judah, Break up your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns (Jeremiah 4:3). Ve-yoreh tsedeq, and rains righteousness: yoreh is the early rain (6:3), and the same letters can be read and teaches, the root of torah.

  • v14 "as Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel… mothers dashed to pieces on top of their children" — Shalman and Beth-arbel are named nowhere else in the Bible. Em al banim, mother on top of children, is Jacob's fear before he met Esau, that he may come and strike me down — the mother on top of the children (Genesis 32:11).

  • v15 "At dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off" — nidmoh nidmah, the verb doubled, as of the mother in 4:5. At dawn, ba-shachar, the hour the people expected the LORD's coming to be sure (6:3).

chapters.title: Out of Egypt I Called My Son
chapters.html:
Hosea 11

When Israel Was a Boy

1When Israel was a boy, I loved him,
and out of Egypt I called My son.

2The more they were called,
the more they went away from them;
they sacrificed to the Baals
and burned incense to carved images.

3Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk,
taking them by their arms;
but they did not know that I healed them.

4I led them with human cords,
with bands of love;
I was to them like those who lift the yoke from their jaws,
and I bent down to them and fed them.

5He will not return to the land of Egypt,
but Assyria will be his king,
because they refused to return.

6The sword will whirl in his cities,
consume his gate bars and devour,
because of their schemes.

7My people are bent on turning from Me;
though they are called upward,
none at all will lift himself up.

How Can I Give You Up?

8How can I give you up, Ephraim?
How can I hand you over, Israel?
How can I make you like Admah?
How can I treat you like Zeboiim?
My heart is overturned within Me;
all My compassion is kindled.

9I will not carry out My burning anger;
I will not again destroy Ephraim;
for I am God and not a man,
the Holy One among you,
and I will not come in wrath.

10They will walk after the LORD;
He will roar like a lion;
when He roars,
His sons will come trembling from the west.

11They will come trembling like birds from Egypt,
and like doves from the land of Assyria;
and I will settle them in their homes,
declares the LORD.

12Ephraim has surrounded Me with lies,
and the house of Israel with deceit;
but Judah still roams with God
and is faithful to the Holy One.

Notes

  • v1 "out of Egypt I called My son" — u-mi-Mitsrayim qarati li-vni. Israel is My son, My firstborn in the LORD's first message to Pharaoh (Exodus 4:22). Matthew reads the verse of Jesus brought back from Egypt: This was to fulfill what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, "Out of Egypt I called My son" (Matthew 2:15), the Hebrew's words; the Greek of Hosea has I called his children.

  • vv2–4 "The more they were called… taught Ephraim to walk… bent down to them and fed them" — a father with a small child. Tirgalti, I taught to walk, from regel, foot, is found only here. Healed is the verb of 5:13 and 6:1. Chavlei adam, cords of a man, are human cords, the kind a person is led by, not a beast's harness.

  • v4 "like those who lift the yoke from their jaws" — ke-merimei ol al lecheihem. Ol is a yoke; the same letters read ul are a nursing child, as in an infant who lives but a few days (Isaiah 65:20), which would make it like those who lift an infant to their cheeks. The father of vv1–3 makes the second reading fit; the vowels of the Hebrew text give the first.

  • v5 "He will not return to the land of Egypt" — 8:13 and 9:3 said they will return to Egypt; here it is Assyria, not Egypt, that will rule. Shuv, return, is used twice: they will not return to Egypt, because they refused to return to the LORD. The Greek has Ephraim settled in Egypt.

  • vv6–7 "because of their schemes… none at all will lift himself up" — v7 is obscure: ve-el al yiqra'uhu, and to the Most High they call him, or to on-high; whether the people call to God or the prophets call the people, the line ends with no one rising.

  • v8 "Admah… Zeboiim… My heart is overturned within Me" — Admah and Zeboiim were destroyed with Sodom and Gomorrah, which the LORD overthrew in His anger and His fury (Deuteronomy 29:23). Nehpakh alai libbi, My heart is overturned, is the verb of that overthrow, He overturned those cities (Genesis 19:25): instead of overturning Ephraim, the LORD's own heart is overturned.

  • v9 "for I am God and not a man… I will not come in wrath" — Balaam's words, God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind (Numbers 23:19). Nichumai, My compassion in v8, is from the same verb as change His mind, nicham: here, because He is God and not a man, His compassion is kindled. Ve-lo avo be-ir, and I will not come in heat, can also be read I will not come into a city, as the Greek has it.

  • vv10–11 "He will roar like a lion… like doves from the land of Assyria" — the lion of 5:14, who tore and went away, roars now to call His sons home; the dove of 7:11, silly and without sense, flying between Egypt and Assyria, comes back trembling.

  • v12 "but Judah still roams with God" — in the Hebrew text this verse is 12:1, and English 12:1–14 is Hebrew 12:2–15; the English numbering is followed. Ve-Yehudah od rad im El is obscure: rad, roams, may be loyal (still walks with God) or restless (still roams free of God), the sense it has in Jeremiah, We roam free; we will come to You no more (Jeremiah 2:31); and qedoshim, holy ones, can be the Holy One, as in 11:9, or the holy ones of heaven.
